items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I mean you listen to early Trane and it’s Prez and it’s Gene Ammons and it’s Dexter you know. I mean they’re all in there.

ctx.x: Nice. Well I’ll read what they said. They should have called you. In regards to your style, “His style is derived principally from that of John Coltrane to which he adds his own rhythmic looseness and lyricism.

Yeah I mean you listen to early Trane and it’s Prez and it’s Gene Ammons and it’s Dexter you know. I mean they’re all in there. I mean everybody’s kind of mixed up in there. But I mean the time that I was probably being more recognized for my soloing would have been with Elvin Jones. With Buddy of course I was known as a soloist but with a big band you’re only going to get a small chunk of space to solo. Right? Maybe one big feature that you get that you know — the suite was something that I kind of inherited…
Can you describe what that was like? Leaving the club after seeing Coltrane?
